docs.title: Senior by default
docs.summary: How a seven-person studio ships with the weight of a much larger one: nobody on the team needs the work spelled out for them.
docs.body:
How a seven-person studio ships with the weight of a much larger one: nobody on the
team needs the work spelled out for them.

## Facts

- Every person who touches the code has shipped real systems and carried real pagers.
- No translation layer between the people who decide and the people who type. The
  person designing the system builds it and owns it.
- Architecture before acceleration: real time spent up front drawing boundaries, what
  the pieces are, where the seams go, what the data is allowed to do.
- Boundaries are made visible in the type system where possible (branded types over
  bare primitives).

## Context

This is the direct answer to "you're small, can you handle it". The constraint is
the advantage, because it removes handoffs, specs written to be misread, and decisions
made by people who never feel their consequences.

docs.title: Software done right
docs.summary: The studio's north star, three words long, published on the site and used as an actual standard in code review rather than a slogan.
docs.body:
The studio's north star, three words long, published on the site and used as an actual
standard in code review rather than a slogan.

## Facts

- **Software**: the artifact is the deliverable, not the demo. The thing that runs at
  3am, that a teammate inherits in two years, that a customer leans on without thinking.
- **Done**: the word people quietly negotiate away, drifting from *finished* to
  *demoed* to *merged* to *technically shipped*. The line: unhappy paths handled, fails
  loudly and recoverably, someone other than the author can run and change it, and the
  thing it replaced is actually gone.
- **Right**: see the source post; the standard "rarely bends."

## Context

The companion argument is that craft is the cheap option that bills later: every
shortcut is a loan, and the interest comes due as the bug you can't reproduce and the
deploy nobody wants to touch. Craft is what makes speed sustainable, because a clean system
is a fast system to change.

Useful in outbound and proposals because it is specific enough to argue with. Source
posts: `craft-as-strategy`, `software-done-right`, `how-we-build` on xors.xyz.

docs.body:
XORS is a boutique software studio that builds custom systems for other companies:
web, mobile, internal tools, data systems. It sells senior execution without agency
overhead, and positions against commodity dev shops rather than competing with them
on price. Roughly 47 products shipped over 8 years. Site: xors.xyz. GitHub org:
`xors-software`.

## Facts

- Not vertical-locked. The work spans DeFi, fintech, healthcare, defence and logistics.
- The public portfolio skews crypto/web3 and enterprise (SushiSwap, Protocol Labs,
  Sentora, Lombard, Glowswap, DCA Markets, O1 Exchange, ZeroCool, Veil Capital,
  Google, State Street), and it is **out of date**. It does not reflect where the
  studio is pointed now. See [[pursue-operator-verticals]].
- Sells "a thinking partner, not just hands". The pitch is judgement, not headcount.
- Everything published carries one line: *software done right*. See [[software-done-right]].

## Context

The studio's whole economic argument is that senior people make fewer expensive
mistakes, so a small team costs less in total than a large cheap one. That claim only
holds if the work is genuinely senior, which is why the roster has no junior tier.

## Open questions

- What is the current headcount split between partners, employees and contractors?
- Is XORS incorporated, and where? What entity signs the contracts?
- What is annual revenue, and what share comes from the top client?

### From gmail (2026-09-17)

ACE is the compliance-automation platform XORS is building for Anodyne/Dia-Foot to pass Medicare DMEPOS (diabetic shoe/insert) audits — covering clinical intake, order review, dispensing documentation, Proof of Delivery, and now a "predispensing" module. XORS ships weekly changelogs to the Anodyne/Dia-Foot stakeholders and is in active pre-release testing as of mid-September 2026.

## Facts
- ACE reads scanned/uploaded clinical documents (foot exam, prescription, PCP note, certifying statement) and runs Medicare compliance rule checks against them, generating a pass/fail audit packet (gmail:"Changelogs For 9/8", 2026-09-09).
- ACE auto-generates the in-office dispensing note and Proof of Delivery (POD), prepopulated from the case data (items, sizes, widths, insert types), with patient signature captured on-device; built to Anodyne's "V9" document layout including bilateral shoe fit and A5514 insert fit forms (gmail:"In office dispensing note and POD", 2026-09-08; gmail:"Changelogs For 9/8", 2026-09-09).
- ACE can build a foot exam note directly from a scanned/uploaded paper nurse checklist or clinical intake form, showing extracted findings for review before applying them (gmail:"Changelogs: Sep 16", 2026-09-16; gmail:"Clinical Exam Intake Form", 2026-09-11/15).
- ACE has a fax-based workflow: outbound reminder faxes (default day 3 and day 7, escalating to a phone call on day 10, configurable by staff) and inbound return-fax matching to the correct case (largely automated but switched off pending validation against real return faxes as of 2026-09-09) (gmail:"Changelogs For 9/8", 2026-09-09).
- ACE has role-based access: clinic staff/receptionists get logins scoped to assigned locations with a patient-status view (no clinical findings/files, no case editing); Anodyne staff administer accounts, locations, and case assignments; clinicians can run intake themselves (gmail:"Changelogs: Sep 16", 2026-09-16).
- ACE has an "audit mode" allowing staff to upload any combination of foot exam/prescription/PCP note/certifying statement and run a full audit without sending a fax (gmail:"Changelogs For 9/8", 2026-09-09).
- ACE integrates with Taika (3D foot-scanning vendor) — releasing an order to Taika rechecks the case against current compliance rules and scan evidence (gmail:"Changelogs: Sep 16", 2026-09-16). See taika.md.
- Clinical corrections in ACE invalidate dependent notes/signatures/packets rather than silently overwriting; the original note is preserved with the correction attached (gmail:"Changelogs: Sep 16", 2026-09-16).
- ACE is migrating its LLM provider from Anthropic direct to Google Cloud (same models — Opus/Fable) specifically so PHI can be handled under a signed BAA; XORS also planned to sign BAAs with Anthropic, Railway, and Anodyne for PHI handling before real patients are onboarded (gmail:"Updates on Release Candidate", 2026-09-10; gmail:"Changelogs For 9/8", 2026-09-09).
- Voice intake/dictation transcription was moved from browser-based to Google Cloud (under signed BAA) (gmail:"Changelogs For 9/8", 2026-09-09).
- ACE has a NetSuite integration for shoe/product codes; as of 2026-09-09 there were 27 unmapped NetSuite codes plus non-Anodyne shoe brand codes to resolve (gmail:"Changelogs For 9/8", 2026-09-09).

docs.summary: On 2026-09-21 Jerry Pan (o1.exchange) asked XORS on Telegram to scope a new product line in onchain options, with no deadline. XORS wrote a reviewed technical scope. The scope recommends an RFQ venue for European BTC and ETH options with fu
docs.body:
On 2026-09-21 Jerry Pan (o1.exchange) asked XORS on Telegram to scope a new product line in onchain options, with no deadline. XORS wrote a reviewed technical scope. The scope recommends an RFQ venue for European BTC and ETH options with full collateral as V1. Its status is READY WITH CLARIFICATIONS.

## Facts

- The client request names three layers: a liquidity layer similar to Deribit, an RFQ marketplace, and an aggregator that gives one quote. References: Derive, Aevo, Ribbon, the Compound VC thesis on onchain options.
- The client also wants structured products: covered calls and put sales (Ribbon model), accumulators and decumulators (Galaxy Digital grids), and sent the Orbit Markets Pivot and Reverse FCN as context.
- The scope lives at `/Users/ahmedpanju/code/xors/o1-onchain-options/technical-scope.md`. The Stage 1 scope, the Stage 2 review (37 findings), and the client brief are in `appendix/`.
- XORS recommendation: one onchain clearinghouse, RFQ as the first trade mode, no margin and no order book in V1. Notes (Reverse FCN, decumulator, fully funded accumulator) come in V2. The Pivot and a margined accumulator at OTC-level strikes need margin (V3).
- Timeline in the scope: Option A (integrate first on a live venue) 3 to 5 months. Option B (own venue) 10 to 14 months with 8 to 9 people. Stage 1 said 7 to 10 months, and the review panel moved it.
- A fully funded accumulator is a live product class (OKX sells one at 1x, weekly observation, 100,000 USDT minimum). The 2x Galaxy row locks $6.49M under full collateral, so expect strikes worse than the Galaxy grid until margin exists.
- The o1.exchange site (2026-09-21) describes o1 as a trading terminal on Base and Solana: terminal, swap, launchpad, cashback tiers, no token on the site. The case-study entry says Base only. The Compound thesis that Jerry shared favors Hyperliquid, so the chain is an open point (Base, Solana, or HyperEVM).
- Only 4 confirmations go to Jerry (first customer, desk relationships, release order, chain). Maker KYC needs and the fixing source are questions for desks in discovery, not for Jerry.

## Context

The scope came from a two-stage process: a technical lead agent wrote it, and an adversarial panel of 8 seats reviewed it. The 2 Critical findings were a blind taker signature (quote hash only) and a false "no admin path to user funds" claim. The final scope corrects both.

## Open questions

- Build the venue, or integrate first? The client must give a written decision.
- Who is the counterparty on the "single quote": the desk that wins, or o1?
- Which entity operates the venue, and for which regions and user classes?
- Which desks does o1 know, and can they quote to wallets with no KYC?
- Will makers accept an oracle TWAP as the fixing, or only the Deribit delivery price?
- Must V1 include a pooled vault with auto-roll (the Ribbon model)?
- Was the scope sent to Jerry, and what did he answer?

### From slack (2026-09-17)

Slopless is XORS's own AI-driven code-security scanning product (CLI + web dashboard), used both as a commercial offering and for benchmarking/marketing (audit contest submissions, open-source scans). Ahmed Panju and Daniil are the primary drivers of the product; Xiangan He weighs in on strategy and marketing.

## Facts
- Slopless is hosted on Railway (frontend on Railway had repeated production outages in May 2026 due to a stuck container with no healthcheck; fixed by adding a /healthz probe + Railway healthcheck and middleware to drop scanner-bot traffic flooding the logs) (slack:#slopless, 2026-05-23).
- Slopless uses a multi-agent / "persona" architecture where different personas search for different bug categories; Daniil raised a concern (2026-05-11) that adding too many narrow personas risks overfitting to known patterns rather than generic adversarial (red/blue-team style) reasoning, and proposed a pre-flight system that spawns personas dynamically based on the target project instead of hardcoding them (slack:#slopless, 2026-05-11).
- Reported performance improvement: Ahmed Panju reported (2026-05-08) that Slopless's "money recall" (dollar value of real bugs caught vs. total available) improved from 4.0% to 17.0% (slack:#slopless, 2026-05-08).
- Benchmarking: Ahmed Panju built a bug-bounty benchmark that replays Slopless against past audit-contest codebases and diffs results against the real judging report — example result: on a "Morpheus" Code4rena contest ($17,500 pool), a pure-LLM scan caught 0 of 9 known bugs, while adding Slither static analysis let Slopless catch 1 Medium-severity bug worth $4,200 (slack:#slopless, 2026-04-15, PR: xors-software/slopless-engine#20).
- Ahmed Panju also ran Slopless against 18 open-source repos as a broader benchmark corpus, and separately found (2026-05-27) that Anthropic's own Claude Code security-review plugin caught a real vulnerability in a code-scanning contest that Slopless missed (n=1 sample) (slack:#slopless, 2026-04-29, 2026-05-27).
- Slopless submits to public audit/bug-bounty contests (e.g., Code4rena) as a growth/credibility strategy, and the team tracks outreach to get people to try Slopless on their own repos via a Notion tracker (slack:#slopless, 2026-05-12 to 2026-05-19).
- Slopless was scanned itself for free by Zellic (via "V12") against the DreamOS brokerage codebase, surfacing critical findings used as a cross-comparison exercise (slack:#slopless, 2026-05-29).
- GTM idea (2026-08-03, #website-lead-magnet-): put a free "Slopless by XORS" vulnerability-scan flow directly on the public site as a lead magnet, ending with a "book a consultation" CTA; also proposed simplifying "Manwe" (an internal component described as overengineered) back into a minimal wrapper around a frontier model, similar to how audits are run manually for o1.exchange (slack:#website-lead-magnet-, 2026-08-03).
- Internal PR-scanning: Slopless is meant to be integrated to run automatically on PRs for XORS's own client codebases (e.g., Carma) as of 2026-04-20 goals (slack:#slopless, 2026-04-20).

## Open questions

- Status of the public lead-magnet scan flow on the website and whether the "Manwe" simplification happened.

docs.title: Lazer Technologies (competitor read)
docs.summary: Toronto product studio, the closest direct competitor to XORS and much larger. Zain Manji is Co-Founder & CEO. They repositioned from digital product studio to AI services and now sell breadth, logos and platform partner badges. A market-up
docs.body:
Toronto product studio, the closest direct competitor to XORS and much larger. Zain
Manji is Co-Founder & CEO. They repositioned from digital product studio to AI services
and now sell breadth, logos and platform partner badges. A market-update email they
sent in September 2026 is the best public read on where agency money moves right now.

## Facts

- **Size**: 80+ senior engineers and designers on their own careers page. Third-party
  data puts total headcount at 170 to 208. XORS is 7. Head-on competition is not an
  option.
- **Their pitch is our pitch.** "Senior only, no junior tier, backgrounds from Apple,
  Google, Coinbase." Seniority is not a XORS differentiator against them. See
  [[xors-studio]].
- Official partner of Anthropic, OpenAI, Cognition, Google and Glean. Partner status
  is their distribution: the platforms route work to them.
- Named clients span Shopify, Stripe, Coinbase, RBC, TD, Wealthsimple, Deloitte,
  Coca-Cola, Home Depot, Cleveland Clinic, Verizon, SKIMS, AG1.
- **PE relationships**: Bain Capital, General Catalyst, GI Partners, Advent
  International, Blackstone, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Dragoneer.
- They state their most repeatable play is "AI SDLC and software factory".
- They sell paid diagnostics as the wedge: an engineering baseline audit against DORA
  before any AI spend, and a build-vs-buy audit scored against commercial platforms.

## What the email taught us

- **Data readiness gates everything.** Their words: many companies need 3 to 6 months
  of foundation work before any application layer. The hardest problem is to move
  knowledge out of people's heads into a system.
- **A large share of what sells is not AI.** Document intake from email, chargeback
  automation, call-centre autofill across un-APIed systems, replacing a spreadsheet
  revenue channel. Zain says it directly: many non-AI problems remain.
- **Every portfolio line is an outcome with a number**, never a technology. "16 weeks
  toward 6." "100+ hours a month." "Cost down roughly 90%." XORS case studies must
  copy this format. See [[case-study-library]].
- **PE is the superconnector.** Private equity appears 6 times in the email: one
  "what we're seeing" bullet, 4 fund names plus OTPP and Dragoneer in the client list,
  and 3 shipped lines. The 2 that carry numbers: BI across "50+ portfolio companies",
  and a whole PE portfolio taken to org-wide AI adoption in 6 weeks. The leverage read,
  that one fund relationship pays out across every company it owns, is ours and not a
  claim Zain makes.
- **The email is referral enablement, not a newsletter.** They send it to executives
  and to people who refer them work, so those people pattern-match better. The ask sits
  at the top, then about 2,000 words of value. They pre-empt the objection in the first
  line: "not AI slop".

## How XORS competes

- Not on seniority, size or logos. On depth in one operator vertical, and on price
  floor. Lazer cannot economically take a $15k to $50k engagement; that is our band.
- The threat is real: Lazer moves down-market through PE portfolios, and PE-owned
  operator companies are exactly [[pursue-operator-verticals]].
- Our own version of the market-read email must be narrow, not a thin copy of their
  breadth. One vertical, deep.

## Open questions

- What is Lazer's actual engagement floor? Assumed above $100k, unverified.
- Do they subcontract overflow work, and is that a channel for XORS?
- Which of their platform partner networks still accept new partners at our size?

## Facts

- Stock line: "I came across your profile and was interested in / impressed by..."

- The ask is always soft and conditional: "Would be great to chat sometime if you're

- Always names ONE genuine hook from the profile, early.
- Three to five short sentences. Never leads with what XORS does.

doesnt sound so AI polished."

The thesis: a partner program at a young platform judges XORS on delivery quality, not
on size, so it fits a 7-person shop where PE procurement does not. See
[[lazer-technologies]] for where the thesis came from.

## Targets

| Platform | Vertical | Stage | Program | Why us |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tennr | Healthcare documents, DME | Series C, $101M | None public | Sells to "DME & Manufacturers", which is [[anodyne-health]] exactly |
| Toma | Car dealerships | Series A, $17M, YC, founded 2024 | None public | Agents plug into dealer software; [[carma]] is the automotive story |
| Decagon | CX agents | Growth | Live, recruits early partners | Lazer already deploys it for clients |
| Avoca | Voice, home services | Early | Live, open application, rev share | Home services is an untouched operator vertical |
| EliseAI | Property management | Series E, $1B+ | Mature ecosystem | Too late. Keep as the shape the others grow into |

## Facts

- Decagon's partnerships page states that an early partner shapes the program itself.
- Avoca's program is a public application with revenue share.
- Tennr raised $101M Series C from a16z, Lightspeed and IVP. Their site lists
  "DME & Manufacturers" as a segment they sell to.
- Toma raised $17M Series A led by a16z, with Y Combinator and Holman participating.
- EliseAI integrates with Rent Manager and PERQ, and raised a $250M Series E.

## Context

Two shapes of opening, and they are not equal. Decagon and Avoca have a form, so you
apply and join a queue. Tennr and Toma run no program, so you reach a founder or a head
of solutions and offer to be first. The second path is slower and worth much more.

Rank by provable overlap, not by how open the door is. Tennr first, Toma second,
Decagon and Avoca third.

**The blocker.** A partner manager forwards XORS to their sales team only with proof in
their language. The public case studies are SushiSwap and Protocol Labs. Fix one case
study before applying anywhere. See [[case-study-library]].

## Open questions

- Does Tennr already use implementation partners privately?
- Which of these accepts a partner without SOC 2?
- Is home services a vertical Ahmed wants, given [[pursue-operator-verticals]] names
  automotive, real estate, medical and agriculture?
- Agriculture has no candidate on this list yet.

docs.title: Engineering standards
docs.summary: The non-negotiable baseline applied to code across the org, enforced by Slopless scanning in CI and by a Claude Code hook before push.
docs.body:
The non-negotiable baseline applied to code across the org, enforced by Slopless
scanning in CI and by a Claude Code hook before push.

## Facts

**Security. Absolute, never allowed:**
- No hardcoded secrets, API keys, tokens or passwords in source.
- No `eval()`, `exec()`, `Function()` or equivalent dynamic execution.
- No SQL string concatenation. Parameterised queries only.
- No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without sanitisation.
- No disabled CSRF/XSS protection, no wildcard CORS in production.
- All user input validated and sanitised. File paths canonicalised and checked for
  traversal. URL inputs allowlisted for SSRF.
- Passwords hashed with bcrypt or argon2, never MD5/SHA1. Session tokens ≥128 bits.
- Never log secrets, tokens or PII. Do log auth failures and permission denials.
- Dependencies pinned to exact versions, no `^` or `~`. No known CVEs.

**Commits**: Conventional Commits, `<type>(<scope>): <description>`. Types: feat, fix,
security, refactor, test, docs, chore, perf. Subject ≤72 chars, imperative mood. Body
explains WHY. One logical change per commit.

**PRs**: title in conventional format; body carries summary, changes, test plan and
scan status. Target under 400 lines changed. Zero CRITICAL findings, zero HIGH without
explicit written justification. Branch naming `slopless/<description-slug>`.

**Scan-fix loop**: run `slopless scan .`, fix CRITICAL/HIGH, re-scan, max 3 rounds.
Past 3 rounds it goes to manual review.

### From slack (2026-09-17)

XORS runs client engineering through Linear for ticketing, a staging-to-production promotion workflow with client demos/changelogs, and has started tightening CI hygiene and pre-commit checks after a cost/runtime incident.

## Facts
- Linear is the standard issue tracker across client projects (Anodyne/ACE, ProDex Labs); team members are expected to claim or create a ticket before starting work to avoid duplicate/colliding work (slack:#anodyne, 2026-09-04; #prodex-labs, 2026-03-17).
- Standard release flow on Anodyne/ACE: ship to staging, run independent internal QA, promote staging -> production, then demo to the client and send a changelog email, roughly on a weekly cadence (slack:#anodyne, 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-16).
- Overlapping PRs are reconciled by one engineer building a single combined branch/PR from the real commits of all conflicting PRs (using merge commits to preserve authorship) rather than a manual rebase chain, with the reasoning and judgment calls documented in a Linear ticket and the PR body (slack:#anodyne, 2026-09-07, PR www-extractor#212, ticket XOR-117).
- After a ~1,300-minute CI runtime spike (Sept 8-10, 2026) traced to how often the pipeline was triggered rather than build failures, the team added a pre-commit hook running lint + typecheck locally, and changed GitHub settings to automatically delete stale head branches to prevent CI buildup (slack:#anodyne, 2026-09-15, PR www-extractor#294).
- Team explicitly discourages excessive/duplicate CI triggering going forward ("for future reference can we please be careful about CI runtime") (slack:#anodyne, 2026-09-15).
- Internally, XORS uses Granola for meeting notes and posts the digest links into project-specific Notion pages after every client call, as part of the outreach/delivery playbook (slack:#biz-dev, 2026-07-29).
- Slopless (XORS's own AI security scanner) is intended to run automatically on PRs for client codebases (explicitly named target: Carma) as an internal quality/security gate (slack:#slopless, 2026-04-20).

Two reasons, and the second is the real one. First, Ahmed's own crypto/web3 depth is
low, so he is selling something he can't speak to with authority. Second, relationship
building, the actual mechanic that closes $15k–$50k engagements, feels authentic to
him in non-technical spaces and forced in technical ones. [[carma]] is the proof it
works.
